The day is decided as the texts say: the nakṣatra (or tithi) should stand for three muhūrtas after sunrise, reaching the saṅgava; if it ends earlier than six nāḍīs after sunrise, the previous day is taken. The solar month must hold up to that mark as well: when the saṅkrānti comes after it, the morning's nakṣatra counts for the month that is ending; when it comes between sunrise and the mark, for neither. It is placed by the same festival engine that places the pañcāṅga's festivals.
